battle.name: 壽陽之戰
battle.brief: 479年十一月北魏三路南下，兵鋒直指淮南重鎮壽春。齊將垣崇祖預築小城、壘堰蓄水，480年二月魏軍攻堰不下，崇祖夜決小史埭，洪水沖營，魏軍溺死數千人，壽陽之圍遂解。卡面羅馬短劍不在壽陽的兵器簿上，它標示的是同一角色：城頭白刃相接時用來刺穿的短兵，壽春守軍握在手中的是環首刀。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 交戰的兩方是北魏與南齊。北魏是拓跋鮮卑建立的北方政權，都平城，疆域北抵陰山、南盡黃河，漢地郡縣與鮮卑八部軍鎮並行，調兵沿用「假王」「公」為一軍之主的舊例：479年冬南征共分八路主將，假梁郡王元嘉即郁豆眷督二將出淮陰，隴西公拓跋琛三將出廣陵，河東公薛虎子三將出壽春，車騎大將軍昌黎王馮熙出義陽，另有郎大檀出朐城、白吐頭出海西、元泰出連口、封延出角城、賀羅出下蔡，尉元與薛虎子討五固義眾。魏軍骨幹是騎兵與甲騎，步兵列於兩翼，攻城另配雲梯、撞車與穴地器械，糧秣自平城、洛陽分批運至前線。南齊是蕭道成於479年四月代劉宋而建的王朝，都建康，中樞設中軍將軍宿衛石頭城，地方以州刺史、郡太守、鎮戍主逐層防守，兵源分禁軍、州郡兵、鎮兵與水軍。壽春是齊方淮南的樞紐，漢置九江郡治此，城西、北、南三面為水所限，肥水在城西北流過，芍陂陂塘在其西南，控淮泗而當南北。齊廷以豫州刺史垣崇祖鎮之，另以徐州刺史崔文仲當鍾離、司州刺史蕭景先備義陽、荊州刺史豫章王蕭嶷遣中兵參軍蕭惠朗領二千人與劉伾緒領千人北援。魏齊隔淮相望，誰守住渡口與城垣，誰就守住這一線。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were Northern Wei and Southern Qi. Northern Wei was the northern state founded by the Tuoba Xianbei, with its capital at Pingcheng, its territory running from the Yinshan range in the north down to the Yellow River in the south, and it governed Han commanderies and counties alongside the garrisons of the eight Xianbei divisions. Troops were raised under an old convention in which a prince by investiture or a duke acted as the head of an army with several generals beneath him, and in the winter of 479 eight commanders were put into the field: the Liang Commandery Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia, also known as Yudoujuan, with two generals through Huaiyin; the Duke of Longxi Tuoba Chen with three through Guangling; the Duke of Hedong Xue Huzi with three through Shouchun; the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Changli, Feng Xi, out through Yiyang; the General of Pacification of the South Lang Datan through Qiushan; Bai Tutou through Haixi; Yuan Tai through Liankou; Feng Yan through Jiaocheng; and Helao through Xiacai, with Wei Yuan and Xue Huzi sent against the insurgents at Wugu. The backbone of the Wei army was cavalry and armoured horse, with infantry on the wings, siege equipment such as scaling ladders, battering rams and tools for sapping the walls, and grain and provisions moved to the front in wagon convoys from Pingcheng and Luoyang. Southern Qi was the dynasty Xiao Daocheng founded in the fourth month of 479 by taking the throne from the Liu Song, with its capital at Jiankang. At the centre it kept a General of the Central Army quartered at Shitou, while locally defence ran down through provincial governors, commandery administrators and garrison commanders, and the manpower came from the imperial guard, provincial and commandery levies, garrison troops and riverine units. Shouchun was the hinge of the Qi side south of the Huai: under the Han it had been the seat of Jiujun Commandery, the city was bounded by water on the west, the north and the south, the Fei ran past it to the north-west and the Shaopi pond lay to its south-west, and it held the Huai and the Si while commanding the road from north to south. The Qi court put Yuan Chongzu, governor of Yu, in command there, with Cui Wenzhong, governor of Xu, at Zhongli, Xiao Jingxian, governor of Si, ready at Yiyang, and Xiao Yi, governor of Jing and Prince of Yuzhang, sending the Colonel of Central Army Xiao Huilang with two thousand men and Liu Pixu with a thousand to the north in support. Wei and Qi faced each other across the Huai, and whoever held the fords and the walls held the line.
people: 北魏這邊，名義上的統帥是年僅十二歲的孝文帝拓跋宏，詔令以他名義發出，朝政由攝政的廣平王拓跋丕與李冲等主持，分道發兵之議出於魏廷。真正到前線指揮的是一批宗室與漢化派將領：出壽春一路的主將是河東公薛虎子，此役失利後他於481年奔齊，齊廷授以官職；假梁郡王元嘉即郁豆眷督兩將出淮陰；隴西公拓跋琛出廣陵；昌黎王馮熙以車騎大將軍督眾接應退軍；前宋宗室義陽王劉昶隨軍而行，魏廷以「奉劉昶恢復宋室」為出兵名號；大陽蠻帥桓誕自請為前鋒，受授南征西道大都督。齊方與北魏在壽陽一線接觸最久的是豫州刺史垣崇祖，他早看準北魏必以壽春為突破口，奉命鎮壽春後即修城、儲糧、積水，築堰蓄水以待。齊高帝蕭道成本人未赴前線，卻在出戰前對垣崇祖說破北魏必以劉昶為辭、必衝壽春。荊州刺史豫章王蕭嶷遣蕭惠朗、劉伾緒分路北援，受阻於義陽、平昌一線；司州刺史蕭景先嚴守義陽，迫魏軍不能西向；徐州刺史崔文仲在鍾離破敵，又派軍主崔孝伯渡淮追擊，朐山戍主玄元度嬰城固守，海路上的崔靈建連夜趕到，以火炬虛張聲勢迫退魏軍。齊廷另遣驍騎將軍王洪範出使柔然約期夾擊，柔然騎兵只抵平城七百里便獵還而回，齊軍未及出師。
peopleEn: On the Wei side the nominal commander in chief was Emperor Xiaowen, Tuoba Hong, who was only twelve years old; the edicts nonetheless went out in his name, and the business of state was conducted by the regency headed by Prince of Guangping Tuoba Pi together with men such as Li Chong, the decision to invade being settled in the Wei court. Those who actually led troops in the field were a mixture of imperial clan members and sinicising commanders. The commander of the column through Shouchun was the Duke of Hedong Xue Huzi, who after the failure at Shouchun fled to Qi in 481 and was given an office by the Qi court; the Liang Commandery Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia, also known as Yudoujuan, went out through Huaiyin with two generals; the Duke of Longxi Tuoba Chen through Guangling; the General of Chariots and Cavalry, Prince of Changli, Feng Xi, was given the task of receiving the withdrawing armies; Liu Chang, the former Prince of Yiyang of the Liu Song, who had fled north years earlier and was treated with marked favour by the Wei court, marched with the army, for Northern Wei fought under the banner of restoring the Song house to him; and Huan Dan, the tribal chief of the Great Yang Man, volunteered for the vanguard and was appointed commander of the western route for the southern expedition. On the Qi side the one who faced the Wei longest on the Shouchun line was Yuan Chongzu, governor of Yu, who had read the Wei plan correctly long beforehand; once the order to hold Shouchun came he set about repairing the walls, storing grain and impounding water, raising a dam and holding the water back in readiness. The Qi emperor Xiao Daocheng himself did not take the field, but before the campaign he told Yuan Chongzu plainly that the barbarians did not understand the turn of fortune and would certainly move their masses to send Liu Chang forward, and that the thrust would come at Shouchun. Xiao Yi, governor of Jing and Prince of Yuzhang, sent Xiao Huilang and Liu Pixu north along separate roads, and they were held up on the Yiyang and Pingchang line; Xiao Jingxian, governor of Si, held Yiyang in strict readiness and kept the Wei from pressing west; Cui Wenzhong, governor of Xu, broke the Wei at Zhongli and then sent the unit commander Cui Xiaobo across the river in pursuit, while the garrison commander of Qiushan, Xuan Yuandu, locked his city and the relief that came up by sea under Cui Lingjian came in the night and put the enemy off with torches. The Qi court also sent the General of Valiant Cavalry Wang Hongfan to the Rouran to arrange a pincer; the Rouran horsemen got within seven hundred li of Pingcheng and then turned back after hunting, and the Qi army never marched out to meet them.
kits: 卡面那柄羅馬短劍（gladius）是帝國軍團步兵的標準佩劍：雙刃直刃，刃長約五十至六十公分，連柄約七十公分，尖端略收而近於鈍，護手小而柄頭綴四顆圓球，通體約一公斤。它的用法從來不是揮砍，而是貼在大盾之後，用盾緣卡住對手的刃，再以短促的刺擊收場。這種劍自共和末期到公元三世紀中葉一直是羅馬步兵的制式冷兵器，三世紀以後被更長的 gladius Hispaniensis 與雙手長劍 spatha 取代，到479年早已退出歐洲軍隊數百年。所以它並不在壽陽的兵器簿上：南朝沒有這種兵器，北魏禁軍用的是環首刀與雙刃直劍。卡面標示的其實是戰術角色而非器物本身——城頭破口與城門後的狹窄地面上的短兵相接，壽春守軍握在手中的，正是同一角色的兵器：魏晉以來成為制式的環首刀，直刃微弧、單刃、刀首環扣。壽陽城頭實際交手的配置是這樣的：兵以弓、弩拒敵於遠，繼以槊、矛、戟壓制登城者，最後才是環首刀與雙刃劍的貼身刺擊；兵具有大盾與小盾，備兜鍪與鎧甲，魏軍甲騎另有馬具與馬鎧。攻城一方備雲梯、撞車、穴地用的通道與堑壕，投石與雷石用於打擊密集隊形；守方備拒馬、木柵與牆頭射孔，並靠堰、小史埭與肥水把水引入敵營。糧秣與物料靠車隊與船，壽春一帶的水路與芍陂水道是齊軍轉運的依托。
kitsEn: The piece on the card, the Roman gladius, was the standard sidearm of the imperial legionary infantry: a straight double-edged blade about fifty to sixty centimetres long and roughly seventy centimetres over all, the point slightly drawn in and close to blunt, with a small hand guard and a pommel finished with four rounded knobs, the whole thing weighing about a kilogram. It was never meant to be swung. It was used behind the large shield, where the rim of the shield caught and turned an opponent's blade and the short thrust finished the business. This sword stayed the standard cold weapon of Roman infantry from the late Republic to the middle of the third century; after that it was displaced by the longer gladius Hispaniensis and the two-handed spatha, and by 479 it had been out of service in European armies for well over a century. It therefore does not appear in the inventory of Shouyang: the southern courts had no such weapon, and the Wei guards carried ring-pommel sabres and double-edged straight swords. What the card marks is a tactical role rather than the object itself. In the short fighting on a breached wall or behind a gate, the blade the Shouchun defenders held in their hands was exactly the weapon of that role: the ring-pommel sabre, straight and slightly curved, single-edged, with a ring at the pommel, which had been the standard form in China since the Wei and Jin. The order of battle on the walls of Shouchun ran like this: bows and crossbows held the enemy at distance, then long spears, halberds and pikes pressed the men who had climbed, and only at the last came the thrusting of the ring-pommel sabre and the straight sword at close quarters. Shields were of the large and the small pattern, with helmets and armour, while the Wei armoured horse had its own harness and its own protection. The besiegers had scaling ladders, battering rams, a covered way for sapping and ditches, and stones and thunder-stones thrown to break up crowded formations; the defenders had cheval-de-frise, timber palisades and firing slots in the wall, and they turned the dam, the small dyke and the Fei water against the enemy camp. Supplies and materials moved by wagon and by boat, and the waterways around Shouchun and the Shaopi channels were what the Qi army relied on to shift them.
tactics: 北魏的打法是多路並進加內應：廣陵一路先動，齊廷聞訊把重兵壓在建康與石頭城，淮南一線吃緊，壽春一路趁隙直取；同時魏人用招撫做內應，義陽有人自稱司州刺史、角城戍主舉城降、汝南太守與龍驤將軍率眾內屬，內外一齊動手。攻城時魏軍築長圍以斷糧道，騎兵在兩翼掠糧、掃援，把主力壓在壽春城西北的堰與小城上，企圖破堰而後自東道進逼大城，並以雲梯、撞車貼到城根，穴地挖通道。守方的三手是垣崇祖的：依高帝事先的叮嚀提早修城儲糧；以大城為犄角而在城西北壘小城、築堰引肥水蓄水，故意示弱，把貪進的敵人引到小城之下蟻附；待敵密集而退路受溝塹所限，夜開小史埭決水，洪水自狹水道奔下，攻城之眾連人馬漂墜，溺死數千人。水退之後齊軍在城頭以弓弩射擊、以雷石打擊殘餘隊形、於缺口用拒馬與木柵堵塞，魏軍退時又乘勢渡河北擊。魏軍的退卻有詔令接應：三月劉昶請退，魏廷詔馮熙督眾迎還假梁郡王元嘉等諸軍，徐徐而退，未至崩潰。齊方的反擊一路追到淮北：崔文仲在鍾離破敵，遣崔孝伯渡淮破茌眉戍；李安民在淮陽以佯敗誘敵，把數千魏騎引入林地，主力自伏兵處趨出，合戰於孫溪渚，魏軍赴清水死者不可勝數；桓康再破敵於淮陽，攻陷樊諧城；垣崇祖趁魏軍摧毀下蔡戍之機渡河北擊。
tacticsEn: Northern Wei fought with several columns moving at once and with work done from inside the enemy lines: the column through Guangling moved first, the Qi court concentrated its main force at Jiankang and Shitou on the news, the line south of the Huai was stretched, and the column through Shouchun took its chance of a direct blow. At the same time the Wei worked through inducement: in Yiyang a man set himself up as governor of Si, the garrison of Jiaocheng came over, and the governor of Runan with a dragon-general led their men in, so that the inside and the outside moved together. When they came to the walls, the Wei built a long enclosing line to cut the supply road, posted horse on the flanks to sweep up grain and intercept reinforcements, and put their strength against the dam and the small city on the north-west of Shouchun, meaning to break the dam and then press on by the eastern road, bringing scaling ladders and battering rams to the foot of the wall and digging a covered way for sapping. The defence rested on three moves by Yuan Chongzu: following the emperor's earlier instruction, he had repaired the walls and stored grain; he took the great city as a pivot and raised a small city on the north-west, damming the Fei and impounding the water, deliberately appearing weak so as to draw the greedy enemy up beneath the small city like ants; and when the enemy had massed below with their retreat cut off by the ditch, he had the small dyke opened in the night and the flood came down through the narrow channel, men and horses swept away and drowned by the thousand. After the water went down the Qi shot from the walls with bows and crossbows, broke up what was left of the enemy with thrown stones, and plugged the breaches with cheval-de-frise and palisades, and when the Wei withdrew they crossed the river in counterattack. The Wei withdrawal was covered by court order: in the third month Liu Chang asked to withdraw, the Wei court ordered Feng Xi to receive the Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia and the other generals and bring them home, and the columns came back in order rather than in a rout. The Qi counterstroke carried the fight north of the Huai: Cui Wenzhong broke the Wei at Zhongli and sent Cui Xiaobo across the river to take the post at Zimei; at Huaiyang Li Anmin gave ground on purpose, drew several thousand Wei riders into the woods, brought his main force out of the ambush to join battle by the Sunxi islet, and the Wei dead in the clear water past counting; Huan Kang beat the Wei again at Huaiyang and took Fanxie city; and Yuan Chongzu crossed the river and struck hard while the enemy were destroying the post at Xiacai.
data: 能站得住的數字有幾條。時間線最清楚：479年十一月北魏三路出師，480年正月隴西公拓跋琛攻拔馬頭戍、馬頭太守劉從戰死，二月魏軍進至壽春城下、決堰大敗，三月劉昶請退、詔馮熙迎還諸軍；480年七月角城戍主舉城降，九月汝南太守與龍驤將軍率眾內屬，481年正月魏軍至淮陽圍角城、角城軍主成買戰死，二月李安民大破魏軍於清水、同月桓康破敵於淮陽攻陷樊諧城、垣崇祖渡河破魏軍，九月五固義眾被平；自出師至收兵歷時約一年零十個月。兵員方面，《南齊書·垣崇祖傳》記魏軍總數為「馬步號二十萬」，這是南朝一方對敵軍的概估，實數遠少於此；同期柔然入寇，《南齊書》作三十萬騎、《資治通鑑》作十餘萬騎，兩說並存，可見南朝估算北方軍力的慣例。壽春小城由數千人守之，《通鑑》作一千人，決堰之後魏軍漂墜塹中，人馬溺死數千人。齊方投入的具體兵力也有數字：蕭惠朗領二千人、劉伾緒領千人北援，李安民遣族弟長文以二百騎為前驅，引入林中的魏騎達數千之眾。距離上，壽春在建康西北約二百公里，肥水在其城西北流過，淮水在城南，鍾離在壽春東南夾淮相望，義陽在壽春西北、淮水上游，兩地相距約三百公里。制度上的數字屬於戰後：484年魏行俸祿制，485年行均田制，486年行三長制。
dataEn: Only a few figures for this war will bear weight. The timeline is the clearest of all: in the eleventh month of 479 the three Wei columns set out; in the first month of 480 the Duke of Longxi Tuoba Chen took the post at Weitou and the governor of Weitou, Liu Cong, was killed; in the second month the Wei reached the walls of Shouchun and were beaten when the dam was cut; in the third month Liu Chang asked to withdraw and the court ordered Feng Xi to bring the generals home. In the seventh month of 480 the garrison of Jiaocheng surrendered, and in the ninth the governor of Runan and a dragon-general led their men in; in the first month of 481 the Wei reached Huaiyang and surrounded Jiaocheng, where the garrison commander Cheng Mai was killed; in the second month Li Anmin routed the Wei at the clear water, in the same month Huan Kang beat them again at Huaiyang and took Fanxie city and Yuan Chongzu crossed the river and broke them; and in the ninth month the insurgents at Wugu were put down, so that the whole business lasted about one year and ten months from the march out to the return. On strength, the biography of Yuan Chongzu in the Nan Qi Shu records the total Wei force as twenty thousand foot and horse, which is a southern estimate of the enemy, well above the real count; for the Rouran incursion of the same years the Nan Qi Shu says three hundred thousand horse while the Zizhi Tongjian says a hundred thousand or more, and the two standing side by side show how the southern court habitually valued northern armies. The small city at Shouchun was held by several thousand men, the Tongjian giving a thousand, and after the dam was cut the Wei were swept into the ditch, men and horses drowning by the thousand. The Qi effort is also given in numbers: Xiao Huilang took two thousand men and Liu Pixu a thousand to the north in support, and Li Anmin sent his cousin Changwen ahead with two hundred horsemen, the Wei riders drawn into the woods running to several thousand. On distances, Shouchun lies about two hundred kilometres north-west of Jiankang, the Fei runs past it to the north-west and the Huai lies to the south of the city, Zhongli faces Shouchun across the river to the south-east, and Yiyang lies to the north-west of Shouchun on the upper Huai, some three hundred kilometres away. The institutional figures belong to the aftermath: in 484 Wei introduced salaries for officials, in 485 the equal-field system, and in 486 the three-chief system for registering households.
cause: 打起來的起因有三層。最外是名分：北魏打的是劉昶的旗號。劉昶是前劉宋義陽王，宗室屠戮中逃奔北魏，魏廷封他丹陽王、屢加厚待，聽到故國滅亡便常涕泣；蕭道成代宋建齊、誅盡劉宋宗室之後，魏廷便以為劉昶恢復宋室為名出兵，藉此把南齊的合法性說成不義之師。第二層是地盤：北魏自太武帝平涼沮渠、得洛陽以來，黃河以南已握在手，但南面隔著淮泗與南齊相望，前一年又取劉宋的青、冀二州與泰山，齊的邊界退到淮水；要打通南北，就必須把淮南與淮北的渡口、戍城一口口吃下，壽春、鍾離、廣陵正是這樣的門戶。第三層是人心與時機：淮北四州久隸南朝，魏廷屢遣間諜誘其歸南，齊方也有反覆接應的安排，義陽、角城、汝南三處內應同時起事；齊朝新立，蕭道成本想乘劉宋覆亡之際北伐，王融、謝朏輩籌劃未成，劉昶乘機勸魏南下，魏廷便把計畫提前。齊廷的牽制手段也落空：蕭道成派王洪範出使柔然約期夾擊，479年八月柔然十餘萬騎抵平城七百里便獵還而回，兩軍未及接觸，壽春便成了魏軍孤注的一擊。
causeEn: The war began for three layered reasons. The outermost is the matter of legitimacy: Northern Wei fought under the banner of Liu Chang. Liu Chang was the former Prince of Yiyang of the Liu Song, who had fled north during the slaughter of the imperial clan and whom the Wei court made Prince of Danyang and treated with repeated kindness, and who was given to tears whenever he heard of the end of his own country; after Xiao Daocheng took the throne from the Song and put the remaining Song clan to the sword, the Wei court marched out in the name of restoring the Song house to Liu Chang, and so presented the new Qi dynasty as an illegitimate usurper. The second layer is territory. Since the Taiwu emperor destroyed the Liang ruler of Guzang and took Luoyang, Wei had held everything south of the Yellow River, yet to the south it still faced Southern Qi across the Huai and the Si, and in the year before it had taken the provinces of Qing and Ji and Mount Tai from the Liu Song, pushing the Qi frontier back to the water. To join north and south, Wei had to take the fords and the garrison towns of the Huai basin one at a time, and Shouchun, Zhongli and Guangling were precisely such gateways. The third layer is the mood of the people and the moment: the four provinces north of the Huai had long belonged to the southern court, Wei repeatedly sent agents to seduce them back south, and Qi had its own repeated arrangements for receiving them, with the three risings at Yiyang, Jiaocheng and Runan beginning together; Qi was a new dynasty, Xiao Daocheng had wanted to march north on the strength of the Song's fall, the plans of Wang Rong and Xie Fei and their like had not ripened, Liu Chang used the opening to urge Wei to the south, and the Wei court brought the plan forward. The Qi attempt to pin Wei down also came to nothing: Xiao Daocheng sent Wang Hongfan to the Rouran to arrange a pincer, and in the eighth month of 479 the Rouran horse, more than a hundred thousand strong, came within seven hundred li of Pingcheng and turned back after hunting; the two armies never met, and Shouchun became a single concentrated stroke by the Wei.
impact: 這一役的果實不在土地，而在兩邊的制度走向。軍事上，南齊守住壽春、鍾離、朐山、角城、泗口一線，淮泗防線不失，北魏未能取得淮南，戰線退回淮水，齊廷得以把新朝初立、百廢待興的局面穩住。齊高帝藉戰後整頓：力行節儉，宮禁器物以銅飾者改用鐵，華蓋除金花爪，後宮櫺檻改飾；清查戶籍以增加租役人口；因荊益一帶群蠻屢叛，於480年分荊、益二州置巴州，以三巴校尉明慧昭為巴州刺史、領巴東太守。北魏這邊的變化更系統化：南征失利後朝野急求改制，484年下詔班俸祿、罷諸商人，戶增調三匹、穀二斛九斗以供官祿，臧滿一匹者死，485年行均田制，486年行三長制整頓戶籍；484年北魏遣李彪回聘南齊，兩國自481年遣使到486年維持約五年無事，487年桓誕反魏奔齊才再啟兵端。對後世而言，494年孝文帝遷都洛陽、495年改姓元氏、499年親征而殂於壺口，都是這幾年平局面積累下來的走向。兵器史上同樣有一條分岔：短刺兵器的技術在中國落到環首刀身上延續了數百年，在歐洲則由短劍走成長劍，兩邊在同一種近身刺擊的邏輯上各自走完了一段。
impactEn: The fruit of this campaign lay not in land but in the direction both states took. Militarily Southern Qi held the line of Shouchun, Zhongli, Qiushan, Jiaocheng and Sikou, the defence of the Huai and the Si was not lost, Northern Wei did not gain the country south of the water, and the front went back to the Huai, which allowed the Qi court to steady a situation still settling after the founding of a new dynasty. Xiao Daocheng used the aftermath to reform: he pressed on with frugality, had the copper fittings of palace fittings changed to iron, the golden flower nails removed from the canopies and the lacquerwork of the inner palace altered; he had the household registers checked in order to enlarge the taxable and liable population; and because the tribes of Jing and Yi rose again and again, in 480 he divided two provinces to create Bazhou, appointing the Inspector of the Three Ba, Ming Huizhao, as governor of Bazhou and administrator of Badong. The change in Northern Wei was more systematic. After the failure of the southern expedition the court pressed on with reform: in 484 an edict established official salaries, dismissed the merchants from the tax privilege, and added three bolts of cloth and two hu and nine dou of grain to each household to pay the officials, with death the penalty for embezzling as much as one bolt; in 485 came the equal-field system; in 486 the three-chief system for registering households. In 484 Wei sent Li Biao back as an envoy, and from the Qi embassy of 481 to 486 the two states kept roughly five years of quiet, broken in 487 when Huan Dan rebelled against Wei and fled to Qi. For later history, the move of the capital to Luoyang in 494, the change of surname to Yuan in 495 and the death of Xiaowen on campaign at Hukou in 499 all grew out of the years of peace that followed this war. In the history of arms there is a parting of the ways here as well: the technique of the short thrusting blade, in China, passed to the ring-pommel sabre and lasted for centuries; in Europe the short sword gave way to the long sword; the two went their own ways on the same logic of stabbing at close quarters.
result: 結果是南齊守住了壽陽。480年二月魏軍攻堰不下，遭決水淹營，溺死數千人，三月劉昶請退兵，魏廷詔馮熙督眾迎還假梁郡王元嘉等諸軍，撤退有接應掩護，沒有崩潰式潰退，淮北新附的角城、汝南等地也隨之失去控制。齊軍乘勢追擊：崔文仲在鍾離破敵後派崔孝伯渡淮擊破魏茌眉戍，李安民在淮陽以佯敗誘敵，把數千魏騎引入林地，合戰於孫溪渚，魏軍赴清水死者不可勝數，同月桓康再破敵於淮陽、攻陷樊諧城，垣崇祖趁魏軍摧毀下蔡戍之機渡河北擊大破魏軍。481年正月角城被圍，角城軍主成買戰死，李安民、周盤龍父子進援，孤軍深入的周盤龍與周奉叔在淮陽擊退魏軍；同年九月五固義眾被魏軍平定，齊方在淮北的內應網就此斷絕。齊高帝在同年遣車僧朗出使北魏議和，車僧朗在魏廷被降人所刺，魏仍為他送喪，雙方自此通使到486年；487年桓誕策動司雍群蠻起義，才引出494至495年、497至499年的第二、第三次齊魏戰爭。壽陽城頭從未出現過羅馬短劍，但那一夜的短兵相接仍有定規：盾在前，刃在下，刺擊收場；握刀的是環首刀，卡面那一柄劍是同一個角色的另一件成品。
resultEn: The result was that Southern Qi held Shouyang. In the second month of 480 the Wei could not take the dam, their camp was drowned when the water was let down, men drowned by the thousand, and in the third month Liu Chang asked to withdraw; the Wei court ordered Feng Xi to receive the Prince by Investiture Yuan Jia and the other generals and bring them home, so the withdrawal was covered and orderly rather than a collapse, and the newly taken places north of the Huai, Jiaocheng and Runan among them, slipped out of Wei control with the army. The Qi pressed the retreat: after Cui Wenzhong beat the Wei at Zhongli he sent Cui Xiaobo across the river and broke the Wei post at Zimei; at Huaiyang Li Anmin gave ground on purpose, drew several thousand Wei riders into the woods, and joined battle at the Sunxi islet, the Wei dead in the clear water past counting; in the same month Huan Kang beat them again at Huaiyang and took Fanxie city, and Yuan Chongzu crossed the river and struck hard while the enemy were destroying the post at Xiacai. In the first month of 481 the Wei surrounded Jiaocheng, where the garrison commander Cheng Mai was killed; Li Anmin and the father and son Zhou Panlong and Zhou Fengshu came up in support, and the two of them, pushing on alone, turned the Wei back at Huaiyang. In the ninth month of the same year the Wei put down the insurgents at Wugu and the Qi network of contacts in the north of the Huai was cut. The Qi emperor sent the Rear Army Colonel Che Senglang as envoy to Wei in the same year to open negotiations; Che Senglang was stabbed at the Wei court by one who had come over, and Wei still sent his body home with honours, and the two states then kept sending envoys until 486. In 487 Huan Dan stirred the tribes of Si and Yong into revolt, and only then did the second and third of the Qi-Wei wars, of 494 to 495 and 497 to 499, follow. The Roman gladius never appeared on the walls of Shouyang, and yet the short fighting of that night still followed a rule: the shield in front, the blade below, the thrust to finish. The sabre in the hand was a ring-pommel dao; the sword on the card is another object of the same role.
